step_1_identify_the_only_5_capped_stack_.claim: The scenario couples exactly two items. Only one of them has any stacking behavior at all, and its cap is 5.

evidence: data/items.json id 3877 passives[0].branches[0] — Spellblade text contains no stack/charge/counter language (100% base AD bonus physical on-hit; Expose Weakness 8%/5% for 4 s; 1.5 s cooldown)
data/item-atoms/3877.json — no stack atom is emitted for Bloodsong; its stack-transform-summon-resource atoms are trap/ward-unit/mana/ammo, none of which is `stack`
data/atoms/items.json objects['3877'] — atom families are damage.*, economy.*, stat.*, timing.cooldown, vision.*; there is NO `stack.gain` atom
data/atoms/items.json objects['3071'] — Black Cleaver IS the only one of the pair carrying `stack.gain` (name 'Carve', values [6.0, 5.0, 6.0, 30.0, 5.0])

step_2_reading_A_stack_count_means_carve.engine_model_quoted: docs/math-foundations.md §2.3(2): "Black Cleaver average stacks (`ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction`): the established model uses a fixed `0.8·max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch) ... the exact Cesàro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C − C(C−1)/(2h)` for `h ≥ C`"

arithmetic.conclusion: Under BOTH engine-sanctioned models the reported Carve stack figure is strictly below the cap for any finite hit count: the constant model returns exactly 4.0, and the Cesàro mean returns 5 − 10/h < 5. The raw cap 5.0 is attainable only in the h→∞ limit, i.e. it is never a correct *modeled* stack count.

step_2_reading_A_stack_count_means_carve.architectural_check: docs/math-foundations.md §5 formula-audit table has no per-event Carve ledger at all: Black Cleaver appears once, as 'Terminus/BC ramps (`average_pen`, `average_reduction`) | Cesàro mean of the per-hit ramp | APPROX'. The engine represents Carve as an *averaged armor-reduction modifier*, not as a per-event integer stack snapshot, so a per-event stack_count on the support stream is not a quantity the documented design produces.

step_3_reading_B_stack_count_belongs_to_.claim: `support_events` is the support-effect stream (support-item procs / ally-support heal-shield events; the ledger's support_shield_received family). The support item in this fixture is Bloodsong.
step_3_reading_B_stack_count_belongs_to_.computation: Bloodsong's Spellblade defines exactly four numeric quantities — 10 s window, 100% base AD bonus physical damage, Expose Weakness 8% (melee) / 5% (ranged) for 4 s, 1.5 s cooldown. None of them is a stack count, and no stack atom is emitted for the item. The correct cardinality of 'Bloodsong stacks' is therefore not 5, not 0, but UNDEFINED — the field has no referent on a Bloodsong support event, and its correct serialization is absence.
step_3_reading_B_stack_count_belongs_to_.provenance_of_the_stale_5.0: data/atoms/items.json objects['3877'] parses Spellblade as values [10.0, 100.0, 4.0, 8.0, 5.0, 1.5] with units [s, percent, s, percent, percent, flat]. The 5.0 in that vector is the RANGED Expose Weakness amplifier percent (8% melee / 5% ranged), not a stack count — a value that coincides numerically with Carve's cap of 5, which is exactly how a stale/leaked field of this shape goes unnoticed.

step_4_rate_sanity_check_on_the_event_in.quote: data/items.json id 3877: Spellblade carries a "{{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack"
step_4_rate_sanity_check_on_the_event_in.arithmetic: A Spellblade-driven support stream can emit at most one event per 1.5 s. Reaching support_events[17] (the 18th event) requires ≥ 17 × 1.5 s = 25.5 s of continuous proccing — longer than any single-rotation fight window the corpus uses. An 18-deep Bloodsong support stream each carrying a stack count is therefore over-generated relative to the sourced cadence, which is consistent with the field (and/or the event) being removed rather than re-valued.

independent_computation.result: 5.0 is not the correct value under ANY reading the cached sources admit: as a Carve figure the documented model yields 4.0 (constant) or 5 − 10/h (exact), never 5.0; as a Bloodsong figure the item has no stack mechanic, so the quantity is undefined. Because the leaf sits on the SUPPORT-effect stream — whose item (Bloodsong) has zero stack semantics — and because the engine's Carve representation is an averaged armor-reduction modifier rather than a per-event stack ledger, the correct state of this leaf is no value at all.

Terminus/BC ramps (`average_pen`, `average_reduction`) | Cesàro mean of the per-hit ramp | APPROX | m(R) convex ⇒ averaging understates ramp damage (Jensen); BC constant = exact mean at ~10 autos, ±20% at extremes

residual_ambiguity: The evidence tree exposes no schema for a support-event record (the golden baseline, scenario fixtures and engine source are outside the permitted export), so the referent of `stack_count` had to be established indirectly. Both admissible referents were computed: as a Carve figure the value must be 4.0 or 5 − 10/h and the engine has no per-event stack ledger to hold it; as a Bloodsong figure the quantity does not exist. Either way 5.0 is refuted, which rules out `old_value_correct` outright. `both_wrong` would only hold if the coupled timeline were intended to expose a per-event Carve snapshot on the support stream — a construct that contradicts the documented averaged-reduction design, so it is rejected in favor of `new_value_correct`.
